title: Localizations of Nagata rings are Nagata
statement: Let $A$ be a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and let $T\subseteq A$ be a multiplicative subset ($1\in T$, $st\in T$ for $s,t\in T$), with localization $T^{-1}A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $T^{-1}A$ is a Nagata ring: it is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T^{-1}A$ the domain $(T^{-1}A)/\mathfrak q$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. In particular each local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and each principal localization $A_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is Nagata.

proof.text: *Noetherian.* $A$ is Noetherian by the definition of a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], so its localization $T^{-1}A$ (with $\lambda:A\to T^{-1}A$, $a\mapsto a/1$, which satisfies (a)-(c) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]) is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. (Stacks leaves this to the reader: the proof of 032U says only 'clear'.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032U (lemma-nagata-localize), proof ('Clear from Lemma 032G'), lines 45724-45727; Definition Tag 032R (definition-nagata), lines 45621-45632

proof.text: *The quotients by primes are localizations of the domains $A/\mathfrak p$.* Let $\mathfrak q\subset T^{-1}A$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-by-prime] (1), $\mathfrak p$ is a prime ideal of $A$ disjoint from $T$, and by (2) of the same lemma, with $\pi:A\to A/\mathfrak p$ and $\overline T=\pi(T)$, a multiplicative subset of the domain $A/\mathfrak p$ not containing $0$, there is a ring isomorphism $\theta:\overline T^{-1}(A/\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\sim}(T^{-1}A)/\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization), lines 3162-3200, and Proposition Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), lines 1379-1385 (the step 032U leaves implicit in 'clear')

proof.text: *N-2.* Since $A$ is Nagata, the domain $A/\mathfrak p$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-n2-domain] (2), applied to $R=A/\mathfrak p$ and $S=\overline T$ (where $0\notin\overline T$ by step 2), the localization $\overline T^{-1}(A/\mathfrak p)$ is a domain which is N-2. The N-2 property [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] is defined from the ring structure alone (fraction field, finite extensions of it, integral closures, finite generation as a module), so it is carried by the ring isomorphism $\theta$ of step 2: $\theta$ extends to an isomorphism of fraction fields $K_1\cong K_2$, a finite extension $L/K_2$ becomes a finite extension of $K_1$ through it, the integral closures of the two rings in $L$ are the same subring of $L$, and a finitely generated module over one ring is finitely generated over the other through $\theta$. Hence $(T^{-1}A)/\mathfrak q$ is N-2.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032U (lemma-nagata-localize), proof: 'Clear from Lemma 032G' (lemma-localize-N, lines 45172-45182)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 1-3, $T^{-1}A$ is Noetherian and all its quotients by prime ideals are N-2, i.e. $T^{-1}A$ is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. The particular cases: $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is $T^{-1}A$ for $T=A\setminus\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $A_f$ is $T^{-1}A$ for $T=\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], both multiplicative subsets.
